basic_info.description:
I’m a Software Engineer with 5+ years of experience building scalable, reliable systems across high-growth technology companies, including Amazon, Microsoft, and Property Finder.

My work sits primarily at the intersection of backend engineering, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and performance. I enjoy taking complex problems—whether it’s handling massive traffic, designing resilient microservices, optimizing cloud infrastructure, or improving system observability—and turning them into simple, dependable solutions.

I work mainly with Java, Go, Python, AWS, Azure, and distributed databases, and I’m particularly interested in systems where scale, latency, reliability, and cost all matter. I’ve worked on high-scale payment and compliance systems, cloud-native services, and infrastructure handling millions of requests.

Beyond writing code, I enjoy understanding why systems behave the way they do and designing them to work better. Recently, I’ve been exploring AI systems, LLMs, RAG, agentic architectures, and AI-powered infrastructure optimization.

I’m always looking for interesting engineering problems, opportunities to build things from scratch, and ways to make software faster, simpler, and more reliable.

projects.title: Homechrome
projects.summary: A handloom textiles business running end to end on software I designed and built solo: Go services on AWS Lambda, semantic product search, an admin back office, and business dashboards fed by an instrumented funnel.
projects.description: A handloom textiles business running end to end on software I designed and built solo — customer storefront, admin back office, and the backend behind both. Shoppers search the catalog in plain language: a sentence-transformer model runs inside the API to match meaning rather than keywords, blended with full-text and fuzzy matching so that "silk bedsheet for a wedding" and a misspelt product name both land on the right shelf. Each query is also classified by intent — material, style, occasion, colour or price — which turns the search box into a running record of what customers actually want. The admin application is where the shop is run: catalog and pricing, inventory, coupons, orders, customers, notifications and reports, all behind role-based access. Alongside it sit the business dashboards. The whole funnel is instrumented — visitor, product view, cart, checkout, payment, repeat purchase — with coupon redemption, order value, UTM attribution, stock-outs, buyer geography and real-user page-speed reported next to it, so pricing and merchandising decisions are made from measured behaviour instead of instinct. Operationally, every request is traced end to end through OpenTelemetry into Grafana Cloud, and the reference ID shown on a customer's error screen is the trace ID, so a support message resolves straight to the request that failed. Underneath: Go on AWS Lambda, an event-driven core, DynamoDB and PostgreSQL, a Next.js storefront, and infrastructure defined as code.

projects.title: ProClip
projects.description: A clipboard manager that helps users to manage their clipboard data(text and images). It ensures that all copied information is securely stored for a period ranging from 30 to 90 days. This feature guarantees that users can access their clipboard history even after restarting their devices.ProClip offers a user-friendly interface with a chronological order of stored data, making it easy to track and retrieve past entries. Additionally, the integrated search bar allows users to quickly find specific items within their clipboard history, enhancing productivity and efficiency

projects.title: Wavelet Trees
projects.description: Wavelet trees are used to separate sound frequencies by decomposing a signal into different frequency bands through a series of filters and decimation. Each node in the tree represents a specific frequency range, with low-frequency components typically on the lower branches and high-frequency components on the upper branches. This process allows for a detailed analysis of the signal's frequency content and its temporal location. We worked on parallelization of the whole process by distributing the subtree process to worker threads and applying optimal compression logic to solve the problem in optimal space and time.

projects.title: Facial Recognition based Attendance Manager
projects.description: Created a face recognising app that could be added to raspberry pie and students can scan their faces and the algorithm will record the entry into a database to maintain the attendance. Used a facial recognition library and trained it with passport images and scaled down the input images to enable the hardware to scan the video input in real time preventing latency or the use of a buffered queue of frames.
